ai.description: This snake reaches 30 cm. It is glossy brown above with a bright orange-red belly, lacking a loreal scale. Its head is indistinct from the neck, and it possesses a single anal plate.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Trachischium guentheri* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or orange belly, which contrasts sharply with the plain, dark brown or blackish dorsal scales.
ai.habitat: *Trachischium guentheri* inhabits moist, high-altitude temperate forests and grassy slopes in the Himalayas, typically found between 1,500 and 3,000 meters elevation.
ai.behavior: The Rosebelly Worm-eating Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time burrowing through leaf litter and soil in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trachischium guentheri* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trachischium guentheri* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Meghalaya, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000m.
